title: Tensor-power sections pull back with inverse-image nonvanishing locus
statement: Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], $n>0$ an integer, and $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$. There exists $t\in\Gamma(Y,(g^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n})$ such that $Y_t=g^{-1}(X_s)$, where $g^*$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and the nonvanishing loci use the germ-outside-maximal-ideal predicate of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. No affineness, quasi-compactness, or ampleness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0892 (morphisms-lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample), proof, equality f^{-1}(Y_t) = X_{f^*t}; tensor comparison is Modules Lemma Tag 01CD (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), and invertibility of powers is Modules Lemma Tag 01CT

proof.text: The tensor-formula pullback and the usual Scheme.Modules.pullback are left adjoints of the same pushforward [def-pc-module-pullback]. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies them. The usual pullback has the proved monoidal structure and unit comparison (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Sheaf, pullbackObjUnitIso). Induct on n, using the binary tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] and this unit comparison, to identify g^*(L^{tensor n}) with (g^*L)^{tensor n}. Tensor powers are invertible by induction on n using the unit and the tensor-invertibility clause of the same lemma. Pull back s via the adjunction unit, restrict from the inverse image of the top open to the top open, and transport along this power isomorphism to obtain t.

At each stalk, extending scalars to the residue field is quotienting by the maximal ideal times the module [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring, clause (1)]. The quotient isomorphism sends 1 tensor v to v modulo that submodule. Consequently the nonvanishing predicate of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] is precisely that the residue value is nonzero. An isomorphism of modules induces an isomorphism of these quotients, preserving whether this value is zero.

Apply the fibre-value clause of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] to L^{tensor n}. The value of the pulled-back s at y is 1 tensor s(g(y)) over the residue-field map. This map is injective since it is a unital field homomorphism. A nonzero vector remains nonzero after field extension: extend it to a basis and take its coordinate functional; after base extension this functional takes 1 tensor v to 1. A zero vector stays zero by bilinearity. Transporting through the power isomorphism preserves zero by step 2. Thus y belongs to Y_t if and only if g(y) belongs to X_s, proving equality of sets.
